review: 305.3-1: base put B's Shock on the stack, so the own_turn variant changed two facts (active player and stack); base now has an empty stack with B having passed priority, the delta changes only the active player, Shock dropped.

scenarios.title: A land can be played only in a main phase of its owner's turn with an empty stack

setup.notes: A has not played a land this turn and has priority. In the stack_not_empty variant the stack holds {'card': 'Shock', 'controller': 'A', 'targets': ['B']}; Shock is not in any other zone.

decisions: A, with priority, attempts to play Forest from hand.

variants.label: main_empty_stack
variants.expected: Playing Forest is legal (can_play true); Forest moves from A's hand directly to the battlefield without using the stack, and no player gets priority in between.

variants.label: combat_phase
variants.delta: The step is beginning_of_combat instead of main1.
variants.expected: Playing Forest is illegal (can_play false): it is not a main phase. Forest stays in A's hand.

variants.label: stack_not_empty
variants.delta: A Shock spell controlled by A targeting B is on the stack.
variants.expected: Playing Forest is illegal (can_play false): the stack is not empty. Forest stays in A's hand.

scenarios.title: A player can normally play one land per turn; Exploration raises the limit

setup.notes: The Forest on A's battlefield was played from hand earlier this turn (lands played this turn: 1).

decisions: A, with priority and an empty stack, attempts to play the Forest in hand.

variants.label: one_already_played
variants.expected: Playing the second Forest is illegal (can_play false): the limit is one land per turn and one has been played. The Forest stays in A's hand.

variants.label: no_land_played
variants.delta: The Forest on A's battlefield was not played this turn; A has played no land this turn.
variants.expected: Playing Forest is legal (can_play true) and it moves to the battlefield.

variants.label: exploration
variants.delta: A also controls Exploration on the battlefield.
variants.expected: Playing the second Forest is legal (can_play true): A may play an additional land this turn. The Forest moves to the battlefield.

scenarios.title: A land play is legal exactly when the lands allowed exceed the lands already played

setup.notes: Exploration allows two land plays this turn. One of the two Forests on the battlefield was played from hand earlier this turn (lands played this turn: 1).

decisions: A, with priority and an empty stack, attempts to play the Forest in hand.

variants.label: allowed_2_played_1
variants.expected: Playing Forest is legal (can_play true): 2 lands allowed is greater than 1 played. Forest moves to the battlefield.

variants.label: allowed_2_played_2
variants.delta: Both Forests on the battlefield were played from hand this turn (lands played this turn: 2).
variants.expected: Playing Forest is illegal (can_play false): 2 allowed is not greater than 2 played. Forest stays in A's hand.

scenarios.title: A land cannot be played past the limit even when an effect permits it

setup.notes: One of the two Mountains was played from hand earlier this turn (lands played this turn: 1). The top card of A's library is Forest. Abbot of Keral Keep costs {1}{R}.

decisions: A casts Abbot of Keral Keep, tapping both Mountains.
Both players pass; Abbot resolves and enters the battlefield.
Abbot's enters trigger goes on the stack; both players pass and it resolves: the top card of A's library (Forest) is exiled and A may play it until end of turn.
A, with priority and an empty stack, attempts to play the exiled Forest.

variants.label: land_already_played
variants.expected: Playing the exiled Forest is illegal (can_play false): the effect permits it, but A has already played a land this turn. Forest stays in exile.

variants.label: no_land_played
variants.delta: Neither Mountain was played this turn; A has played no land this turn.
variants.expected: Playing the exiled Forest is legal (can_play true); it moves from exile to the battlefield.

scenarios.title: A land cannot be played on another player's turn

setup.notes: A has not played a land this turn. B is the active player in main1, the stack is empty, and B has passed priority, so A holds priority.

decisions: A, holding priority with an empty stack during B's main phase, attempts to play Forest from hand.

variants.label: opponents_turn
variants.expected: Playing Forest is illegal (can_play false): it is not A's turn. Forest stays in A's hand.

variants.label: own_turn
variants.delta: A is the active player instead of B (main1, empty stack, A holding priority).
variants.expected: Playing Forest is legal (can_play true) and it moves to the battlefield.

scenarios.title: A land put onto the battlefield by an effect does not count as the land played this turn

setup.notes: A has played no land this turn. Rampant Growth costs {1}{G}.

decisions: A casts Rampant Growth, tapping both Forests.
Both players pass; Rampant Growth resolves: A searches for a Forest and puts it onto the battlefield tapped.
A, with priority and an empty stack, attempts to play a Forest from hand.

variants.label: put_by_effect
variants.expected: The Forest from the library enters tapped without counting as a land played. Playing the Forest from hand is legal (can_play true) and it moves to the battlefield.

variants.label: played_from_hand_first
variants.delta: Instead of casting Rampant Growth, A plays one Forest from hand first, then attempts to play the second Forest from hand.
variants.expected: The first land play is legal. The second land play is illegal (can_play false): one land has been played this turn. The second Forest stays in A's hand.

scenarios.title: A land with a basic land type has that type's mana ability regardless of its text

setup.notes: Dryad Arbor has only reminder text but is a Forest Dryad land creature, under A's control since before the turn began. Giant Growth costs {G}.

decisions: A casts Giant Growth targeting Grizzly Bears, paying {G} by tapping Dryad Arbor for mana.
Both players pass; Giant Growth resolves.

variants.label: forest_type
variants.expected: Dryad Arbor taps for {G}: Giant Growth is cast (can_play true) and Grizzly Bears is 5/5 until end of turn.

variants.label: no_basic_type
variants.delta: A controls Wastes (a basic land without a basic land type, whose own ability adds only {C}) instead of Dryad Arbor.
variants.expected: Wastes can only add {C}; Giant Growth cannot be cast (can_play false) and stays in A's hand; Grizzly Bears stays 2/2.

scenarios.title: Setting a land's subtype to a basic land type replaces its old types and abilities, while adding types keeps them

setup.notes: Bayou is a Swamp Forest land and taps for {B} or {G}. Blood Moon makes nonbasic lands Mountains. Giant Growth costs {G}.

decisions: A attempts to cast Giant Growth targeting Grizzly Bears, paying {G} by tapping Bayou for mana.
If the cast is legal, both players pass and Giant Growth resolves.

variants.label: blood_moon
variants.expected: Bayou is a Mountain only: it lost Swamp and Forest and their mana abilities, and taps only for {R}. Giant Growth cannot be paid (can_play false) and stays in A's hand; Grizzly Bears stays 2/2.

variants.label: no_blood_moon
variants.delta: Blood Moon is not on the battlefield.
variants.expected: Bayou is a Swamp Forest and taps for {G}; Giant Growth is cast and resolves, Grizzly Bears is 5/5 until end of turn.

variants.label: urborg_instead
variants.delta: Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth is on A's battlefield instead of Blood Moon.
variants.expected: Bayou keeps Swamp and Forest (Swamp is added in addition) and keeps its mana abilities; it taps for {G}. Giant Growth is cast and resolves, Grizzly Bears is 5/5 until end of turn.

scenarios.title: A card that is a land and another type can be played only as a land, never cast

setup.notes: Dryad Arbor is a land creature card. A has played no land this turn.

decisions: A, with priority and an empty stack, attempts to cast Dryad Arbor as a creature spell, tapping both Forests.

variants.label: cast_as_spell
variants.expected: Casting Dryad Arbor is illegal (can_play false): a land card cannot be cast. It stays in A's hand and the Forests stay untapped.

variants.label: play_as_land
variants.delta: A attempts to play Dryad Arbor as a land instead of casting it.
variants.expected: Playing Dryad Arbor as a land is legal (can_play true); it moves to the battlefield without using the stack.
